inline.s: Every affliction is the foundation of wisdom. If we sink deeply into our afflictions, or try to repress them, we will in the end bind ourselves in our own cocoon and create still more problems for ourselves. But if we can turn and look directly at these afflictions, then those very things we dread will harm us gradually transform into the most powerful allies for meditation that we could hope for.
Afflictions are not our enemies; they are our friends.

This is a fact that is hard to accept, yet whenever you shrink back and cannot agree, think of the peacock. Poisonous plants are not to the palate’s liking, but should a peacock truly swallow them, it can turn that poison into its bright and splendid plumage.

In this final lesson of the practice, we have seen what meditative remedies one may apply when facing the most fearful and most painful experiences. Having examined these practices, we come to understand that every affliction which makes us retreat, take fright, or feel fragile holds an equal power to make us stronger, more confident, more open, and more able to receive the limitless possibilities of our own Buddha-nature.
